subject: Sapphire integration: batching, caching & quantization orchestration
raw:
From: Sasha Lee <sasha@novaprod.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sapphire - looking for a practical cost/perf plan

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We're moving toward a soft launch and need a compact, prioritized plan to get token cost under control without blowing up p99 latency. Key constraints:
- Live traffic is chat-style (avg prompt 140 tokens, reply 60 tokens),
- Peak qps ~30 (expected to double in month 1),
- Security: must stay in our VPC for private deployment, and we need a clear quant profile for now.

Can Redwood help map batching/caching/quant settings into a 2-week implementation sprint we can share with SRE? We also attached the initial scope spreadsheet you asked for.

Appreciate a short checklist we can follow.

—Sasha
[Attachment: initial_scope.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)]

Subject: Re: Sapphire - batching/caching/quant orchestration plan

Sasha — thanks, this is exactly the kind of framing we prefer. I drafted a focused 2-week plan below that balances near-term cost wins with safe latency SLOs. Attaching the Redwood playbook and a canary template.

High-level approach (2 weeks):
1) Week 1 — Quick wins (safe, low-risk)\  - Enable automatic prefix/KV caching for chat sessions (expected 10–25% token reduction)\  - Configure per-route batching with conservative limits (max batch latency budget 30ms)\  - Test 8-bit quant profile on a small subset of requests (non-production)
2) Week 2 — Controlled rollout & tuning\  - Canary: route 10% of traffic to quantized instances, monitor latency and regeneration rate\  - Adjust batch sizing policy by request size distribution (target throughput uplift)\  - Gradual increase of cache TTL where output quality holds

Action items (owners):
- Stephanie: run an initial micro-benchmark with Sapphire sample prompts (today)
- Rishi: propose quant profiles and perf numbers (tomorrow)
- Laura: schedule canary window and define rollback thresholds (by EOD Wed)
- Monica: prepare onboarding checklist and doc links for SRE

Attachments:
- redwood_cost_tune_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook, ~1.2MB)
- canary_rollout_template.docx (template)

Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call Wednesday 10:00am PT to lock on thresholds. Does that work?

Best,

Subject: Re: Sapphire - batching/caching/quant orchestration plan

Quick notes from the perf side so SRE has concrete numbers to test with:
- Quant profiles: start with q4_8 and q4_8_dynamic for CPU fallback; expected token cost reduction ~30–40% vs fp16 with minimal quality delta on conversational prompts.
- Benchmark targets (per-host): baseline p50 12ms token, p95 110ms token; with batching we can drive p50 lower but watch p95 tail — keep batch TTL <= 30ms to protect tails.
- KV cache: recommend prefix caching keyed by conversation_id + user_id. TTL 4h initial, increase to 24h if re-gen stays <1.5%.
- Routing policy: Primary: low-latency pool (fp16) for interactive; Overflow: quantized pool for cost-sensitive async calls (e.g., embeddings/reranks).

I'll drop synthetic perf numbers into the shared drive and attach a short CSV.

—Rishi

Sasha — looping in the proposed canary gates so your SRE can implement them:
Canary gate checklist:
- Traffic split: start 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 3 maintenance windows\- Latency gates: p95 must not increase > 15% from baseline for 15 consecutive minutes\- Error gates: 5xx rate exceeds 0.5% -> automatic rollback\- Quality gates: regenerations >1.5% vs baseline -> pause and review\- Observability: token-level cost dashboard, per-route p95, and a quick alert for model fallback events

I'll own the rollout schedule and coordinate the maintenance windows with your ops team. If Wednesday 10am PT works for everyone, I'll send an invite with the runbook and the DocuSign link for the reserved capacity amendment (if you want to lock in dedicated pools).

Thanks — Laura
